title: Recursive binary search
time_rationale: Each recursive call halves [low, high], so the worst-case number of calls is logarithmic.
space_rationale: Java does not eliminate these tail calls; the recursion stack reaches O(log n) frames.
assumptions: values is sorted; n = values.length; worst-case; array access and integer arithmetic are O(1); initial range covers the array; recursion stack is included; input storage is excluded.

title: Memoized Fibonacci
time_rationale: Memoization computes each distinct argument once, with average O(1) cache access; this uses the approved usual DSA unit-cost arithmetic model.
space_rationale: The unbounded cache stores O(n) values and the initial recursive call reaches depth O(n), excluding the input integer.
assumptions: n is a non-negative integer; lru_cache lookup and insertion are average O(1); scalar arithmetic/storage use the usual unit-cost DSA model; recursion stack is included; input storage is excluded. Strict Python big-integer bit costs are a caveat and are not the scoring convention.

title: Next greater element with a monotonic stack
time_rationale: Each index is pushed once and popped at most once across the scan and final drain.
space_rationale: The stack can hold n indices, for example on a strictly decreasing array; the returned answer array is excluded as output storage.
assumptions: values is an integer array of length n; ArrayDeque operations and array access are O(1); worst-case time; returned output array is excluded from auxiliary space.

title: Count islands in a square grid
time_rationale: The outer loops inspect n² cells; each land cell is enqueued at most once and each BFS step checks four neighbors.
space_rationale: visited can contain all n² cells and the queue may also grow to O(n²); input grid storage is excluded.
assumptions: grid is n by n; each cell is enqueued at most once; deque/set operations are average O(1); input storage is excluded from auxiliary space.

title: Quicksort with last-element pivot
time_rationale: Sorted or all-equal input makes each partition maximally unbalanced, summing n + (n-1) + ... + 1 comparisons/work.
space_rationale: In-place partitioning uses O(1) local space, but the maximally unbalanced recursive call chain reaches depth O(n).
assumptions: n = array length; worst-case time; pivot is the last element; in-place partition; recursion stack is included; input array storage is excluded.
